transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I... I came because things with my in-laws aren’t just normal arguing. They’re using the church altar, the parish committee... trying to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for the family.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by your in-laws trying to push you out and make people forget what you've done? Do you feel they are conspiring against you in a way that others don't recognize?

Yes... I think they are. It’s not just family disagreement. They use the church, the altar, the parish committee... places where people listen. They want to push me aside and make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you believe that your in-laws are specifically targeting you with harmful intentions, even if others don’t see it the same way?
Yes… I do. I know they’re not just arguing with me. They’re using the altar, the parish committee… trying to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you feel that your in-laws’ actions against you are part of a larger, organized plan that you can’t see completely, but you know is happening?
Yes… I don’t see all of it, but I know it’s happening. It’s more than arguing. They’re using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… to make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Can you explain how you know that your in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee against you? Have you noticed specific signs or events that led you to this conclusion?

I just… I can tell by how things are said there. At the altar, in the parish committee, it feels like they’re turning people away from me. It isn’t just arguing at home. They’re trying to push me out, make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you feel certain that your in-laws’ actions are part of a deliberate, hidden effort to harm you, even if there’s no clear proof that others can see?

Yes… I feel certain. I came in because I knew it wasn’t just arguing with my in-laws. They were using the altar, the parish committee… trying to push me out, make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you feel that you are the only one who can see this plan against you, or do others also recognize that your in-laws are using the church and parish committee to harm you?

I think… I’m the one seeing it clearly. Other people don’t want to say it, maybe. But I know my in-laws aren’t just arguing with me—they’re using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Have you talked to anyone else about these concerns, and if so, how have they responded when you’ve shared your thoughts about your in-laws’ plan?

I’ve mentioned it a little… not to many people. They don’t really understand, or they act like it’s just family arguing. But I know it’s more than that. That’s why I came in. My in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… to make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Even though others don’t share your belief, can you explain why you are so sure that your in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee against you?

Because it’s not just… normal family arguing. I can feel the way they’re doing it, through the altar and that committee. It’s like they’re trying to push me out, make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family. That’s why I came in.
Even though others don’t see it the way you do, do you believe your understanding of what’s happening is the only correct one?

Yes… I do. I know how it sounds, but I came in because I knew they weren’t just arguing with me. My in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… to make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Even when people you trust say they don’t see this happening, do you still believe with absolute certainty that your in-laws are using the altar and parish committee against you?
Yes. I know they don’t see it, but I’m sure. It’s not just arguing… they’re using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Have you ever had experiences where you felt certain about something that others said wasn’t true, even when there was no clear evidence supporting your belief?

Yes… I suppose. This with my in-laws. I know people say there’s no proof, but I came in because I knew it wasn’t just arguing. They were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Even though there is no clear proof and others don’t share your belief, do you still hold it with complete certainty?

Yes. I know people say there’s no clear proof, but I’m certain. They weren’t just arguing with me… my in-laws were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make everyone forget what I’ve done.
Even though there is no clear proof and others don’t share your belief, do you still hold it with complete certainty?

Yes… I do. I know people don’t see it the way I do, but I came in because I knew it wasn’t just arguing. They’re using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… to make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
